md_description: This DAG represents a combined genomics and metabolomics workflow for fungi producing secondary metabolites. It covers fungal biomass processing, genomic DNA extraction, whole-genome sequencing, biosynthetic gene cluster discovery, gene-level cluster annotation, and chemical isolation plus analysis of secondary metabolites. The resulting data support discovery of novel bioactive compounds and reconstruction of the genetic architecture underlying their biosynthesis.

fungal_biomass.reasoning: The fungal_biomass node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic identity/origin fields for the starting biological material: what fungal organism/material it came from, how it was obtained, and basic source context needed to interpret downstream DNA and metabolite workflows. I excluded any extraction, sequencing, or analytical settings because those belong to downstream Process/Capture nodes. I also avoided sample identifiers that could overlap with root-level entity metadata if already generated elsewhere, and I did not include biomass properties that are actually measured outputs of later processing (e.g., DNA yield, metabolite concentration).

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the fungal biomass specimen used as the starting material in this workflow; use a stable sample code such as FBM_001. This is assigned once at collection/receipt and should link the biomass to all downstream DNA and metabolite preparations.
Scientific name of the fungal organism or operational taxonomic unit represented by the biomass, recorded at collection or after taxonomic confirmation; format example: Aspergillus terreus.
Internal strain or isolate identifier if the biomass comes from a cultured fungal strain, recorded at the point the biological material is registered; format example: ATCC 12345 or isolate FUNG-17.

Origin of the fungal material represented by this entity, describing the biological source context rather than any processing step; examples include cultured mycelium, fruiting body tissue, or environmental isolate biomass.
Physical form of the fungal material at collection/receipt before any DNA or metabolite processing; examples include wet biomass, dried biomass, lyophilized tissue, or pelletized mycelium.
Date when the fungal biomass was collected or received for this workflow, used to place the entity in time; format YYYY-MM-DD.

High-level natural or cultivation origin of the fungal biomass, recorded to help interpret secondary-metabolite potential; examples include soil, plant-associated, marine-associated, or laboratory culture.

dna_extraction.reasoning: The dna_extraction node is a Process, so I included only how the extraction was performed and the key process outcome needed for reproducibility and quality assessment. I focused on lysis chemistry, purification method, yield, purity, and operator/context details that belong to the transformation step itself. I excluded DNA identity/source fields because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded library, sequencing, or read-quality fields because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating any sample identifiers that may already exist on the fungal biomass entity.

md_schema.descr: Primary lysis approach used to break open fungal cells during genomic DNA extraction; record the method used at the extraction step, such as bead beating, enzymatic digestion, or chemical lysis.
Commercial kit or extraction protocol name used to purify genomic DNA from fungal biomass at the extraction step; format example: Qiagen DNeasy Plant Mini Kit.

Major reagent system or solvent/buffer chemistry used for DNA purification during extraction, recorded at the process step; examples include CTAB-based, silica-column-based, phenol_chloroform-based, or magnetic-bead-based workflows.

Temperature in degrees Celsius used during the extraction process when lysis or incubation was actively controlled; report the setpoint or incubation temperature, typically in the range 4-95 Celsius depending on protocol.
Total duration in minutes for the active DNA extraction workflow or main lysis incubation measured at the process step; typical range is 10-240 minutes depending on protocol complexity.

Amount of purified genomic DNA recovered from the extraction step, measured after final cleanup and before library preparation; report in nanograms, typically from tens to thousands of ng depending on biomass input.
A260/A280 absorbance ratio measured on the purified DNA after extraction and cleanup to assess protein contamination; typical acceptable range is about 1.7-2.0 for genomic DNA.
Qualitative assessment of extracted DNA integrity immediately after purification, used as a process quality indicator before library preparation; judge whether the DNA is suitable for sequencing.

genomic_dna.reasoning: The genomic_dna node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the purified DNA object itself, not extraction protocol details or later library/sequencing settings. The most useful entity-level fields here are identity linkage, source lineage from the biomass, concentration, size/integrity, and storage conditions, because these describe what the DNA material is and its readiness for downstream library preparation. I avoided repeating extraction method, kit, or yield fields because those belong to the dna_extraction Process node, and I avoided any library preparation fields because those belong downstream. I also kept sample identifiers distinct and non-duplicative relative to any root-level entity metadata.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the purified genomic DNA aliquot used for library preparation; use a stable sample code such as gDNA_001. This is assigned after extraction and links the DNA entity to downstream library construction.
Identifier of the upstream fungal biomass sample from which this genomic DNA was purified, used to maintain provenance across the workflow; format example: FBM_001.

Measured concentration of the purified genomic DNA entity after extraction and cleanup and before library preparation; report in nanograms per microliter, typically in the low single digits to hundreds of ng/ul.
Total mass of purified genomic DNA available in the aliquot at the time it is entered into library preparation; report in nanograms, typically from tens to thousands of ng.

Representative fragment size of the purified genomic DNA entity before library preparation, assessed from gel or fragment analysis; report in base pairs, typically ranging from several kilobases to high molecular weight DNA.

Numeric integrity assessment of the purified genomic DNA entity measured after extraction and before library prep, if available from an instrument such as TapeStation or Bioanalyzer; typical range is 1-10.
Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the purified genomic DNA entity is stored prior to library preparation; examples include -20 or -80 Celsius.
Buffer or solution used to store the purified genomic DNA entity before library preparation, such as TE buffer or nuclease-free water.

library_prep.reasoning: The library_prep node is a Process, so I included only how genomic DNA was converted into a sequencing library: fragmentation approach, adapter/index strategy, target insert size, input amount, amplification/cycle settings, and a process-quality indicator. I excluded upstream DNA intrinsic properties beyond what is consumed by the process, and I excluded downstream library entity properties such as file outputs or read data because those belong to the seq_library Entity and raw_fastq Signal nodes. I also avoided duplicating any identifiers already defined on the DNA entity, and I did not include sequencing instrument settings because those belong to the Capture node.

md_schema.descr: Amount of purified genomic DNA input to the library preparation process, measured at the start of the workflow step; report in nanograms, typically from 0.1 to 1000 ng depending on protocol.

Method used to shear or enzymatically fragment genomic DNA during library preparation, recorded at the process step; examples include mechanical shearing, transposase-based fragmentation, or enzymatic fragmentation.
Desired average DNA insert size after fragmentation and size selection during library preparation, measured in base pairs; typical range is about 200-1000 bp for short-read sequencing libraries.
Library adapter or kit name used to convert fragmented DNA into sequencing-compatible molecules at the preparation step; format example: Nextera XT DNA Library Prep Kit.

Indexing or barcode scheme applied during library preparation to distinguish samples in sequencing runs, recorded as the preparation strategy; examples include single indexing, dual indexing, or combinatorial indexing.
Number of PCR amplification cycles used during library enrichment at the library preparation step; typical range is 0-18 cycles depending on input DNA and protocol.
Whether a size-selection step was applied during library preparation to narrow the insert distribution before sequencing; this is assessed at the end of the preparation process.
Total mass of prepared sequencing library recovered at the end of library preparation, measured before loading onto the sequencer; report in nanograms, typically from a few ng to several hundred ng.

Boolean indication of whether the prepared library met internal quality-control criteria for sequencing readiness at the end of the library preparation process, such as correct size distribution and sufficient concentration.

seq_library.reasoning: The seq_library node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the prepared library itself: identity/provenance, library type, insert-size distribution, adapter/index composition, concentration, and storage/readiness. I excluded library preparation protocol parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded sequencing instrument settings because those belong to the downstream Capture node. I also avoided file-level properties, since the raw file outputs are represented later by the raw_fastq Signal node, and I did not repeat any identifiers that would duplicate upstream sample IDs.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared sequencing library entity used for whole-genome sequencing; use a stable code such as LIB_001. This is assigned after library preparation and before loading onto the sequencer.
Identifier of the upstream purified genomic DNA sample from which this sequencing library was prepared; format example: gDNA_001.

Type of sequencing library represented by this entity at the time it is submitted for sequencing, describing the construct class rather than the protocol; examples include paired-end genomic DNA library or mate-pair library.

Average DNA insert size of the prepared library entity measured after size selection and before sequencing; report in base pairs, typically in the 200-1000 bp range for short-read whole-genome libraries.

Adapter or index sequence composition associated with the prepared library entity for multiplex sequencing, recorded as the final barcode design; use a sequence label or barcode name such as i7-001/i5-001 when available.
Measured concentration of the prepared sequencing library entity after final cleanup and before sequencing loading; report in nanograms per microliter, typically low single digits to tens of ng/ul.

Qualitative assessment of the prepared library's size distribution and suitability for sequencing, measured on the finished library entity before it enters the sequencer; typical categories reflect whether the profile matches the intended insert distribution.
Storage condition of the prepared sequencing library entity prior to loading onto the sequencer, recorded as the storage state at handoff; examples include 4 C short-term or -20 C frozen storage.

wgs_capture.reasoning: The wgs_capture node is a Capture node, so I included only the instrument configuration and measurement-session settings that were actively controlled during whole-genome sequencing: platform identity, run mode, read layout, cycle configuration, loading parameters, and core quality output metrics. I excluded sample/library intrinsic properties because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, and I excluded file-level properties such as FASTQ format or file size because those belong to the downstream raw_fastq Signal node. I also included hardware manufacturer/model/serial context as required for capture nodes, while avoiding software-specific process fields that do not belong here.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for the whole-genome sequencing capture session, recorded as the hardware vendor controlling the measurement; example: Illumina.
Model name of the sequencing instrument used for the whole-genome sequencing capture session; example: NovaSeq 6000. Record the platform actually used to generate the raw reads.
Instrument serial number for the sequencing system used in this capture session, recorded to uniquely identify the hardware unit; format example: NSQ1234567.

Unique identifier of the sequencing run/session that produced the raw genomic reads; use the instrument or facility run code such as RUN_2024_001. This links one capture session to its resulting raw data.
Read structure configured for the sequencing capture session, indicating how reads were generated from each library molecule; examples include paired-end or single-end layout.
Configured read length in base pairs for each end of the sequencing capture session, measured as the intended cycle output per read; typical short-read whole-genome values are 75-300 bp.
Flow cell or cartridge type used during the capture session, recorded as the sequencing consumable configuration that defines output capacity; example: S4 flow cell.

Loading concentration of the prepared library applied to the sequencer during capture, reported in picomolar and set at run setup; typical range is roughly 1-20 pM depending on platform and library complexity.
Number of lanes or equivalent physical output partitions used in the capture session, recorded at run setup; use the platform-specific count when applicable.
Total number of sequencing cycles configured for the capture session, reflecting the active read configuration; typically 150-600 cycles for short-read paired-end runs.
Date on which the whole-genome sequencing capture session was initiated or completed, recorded to timestamp the instrument run; format YYYY-MM-DD.

Percentage of bases in the sequencing run with Q30 or higher, used as a run-level quality indicator for the capture session after the instrument run completes; typical good runs exceed 75 percent depending on platform and chemistry.

Observed cluster density or equivalent loading density on the sequencing instrument, measured during the capture session as a run-quality indicator; report using the platform-specific unit, typically clusters per square millimeter for Illumina systems.

raw_fastq.reasoning: I removed the colliding field read_length_bp because it was already generated for an upstream DAG step and the schema must remain non-duplicative across the workflow. For the raw_fastq Signal node I kept only raw-file properties and technical file-level quality/traceability fields. I retained file identity, format, size, read count, paired-end status, base-quality summary, GC content, storage location, and checksum because these describe the signal artefact itself rather than capture settings or downstream interpretation.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw FASTQ file or file pair produced by the sequencing run; use a stable file code such as FASTQ_001 or FASTQ_001_R1/R2 for paired-end data. This identifies the raw data artefact itself.
Digital file format of the raw sequencing signal artifact, recorded at the file level after capture; for this node it is typically FASTQ.
Size of the raw FASTQ file in bytes, measured from the stored digital artefact after sequencing transfer and compression; useful for integrity checks and data management.

Total number of sequencing reads represented in the raw FASTQ artifact, counted from the file contents after demultiplexing or file generation; typically ranges from millions to hundreds of millions for whole-genome sequencing.
Whether the raw FASTQ signal represents paired-end data with one or two companion read files, recorded at the file artifact level.

Average Phred quality score across bases in the raw FASTQ file, calculated from the file contents as a technical signal quality metric; typical values for good short-read data are in the high 20s to mid 30s.

Percentage of bases in the raw FASTQ data that are G or C, computed from the stored reads as a technical composition metric; use this as a file-level quality/context indicator rather than a biological interpretation.
File system path or object-storage URI where the raw FASTQ data are stored after sequencing transfer; example formats include /data/run1/sample.fastq.gz or s3://bucket/path/sample.fastq.gz.
MD5 checksum of the raw FASTQ file used to verify data integrity after transfer or storage; format example: 32-character hexadecimal digest.

genome_assembly.reasoning: The genome_assembly node is a Process, so I included only assembly workflow parameters and process-level outcomes: assembler details, k-mer/normalization settings, contig/scaffold statistics, and assembly quality indicators. I excluded raw read properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the assembled genome object itself because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided the previously generated field read_length_bp by not repeating read configuration; instead I focused on assembly-specific metrics such as contig counts, N50, and completeness that characterize the transformation process.

md_schema.descr: Name of the genome assembly software used to reconstruct contigs and scaffolds from raw sequencing reads at this process step; example: SPAdes.
Version of the genome assembly software used during the assembly process; example: 3.15.5. Record the exact version to enable reproducibility.

K-mer sizes configured for the assembly process, recorded as the set of word lengths used by the assembler; example values might include 21,33,55. This is a process parameter measured at assembly time.

Number of contigs produced by the assembly process, counted after contig generation and before any downstream curation; typical values vary from tens to thousands depending on genome complexity and read quality.
Number of scaffolds produced by the assembly process if scaffolding was performed, counted after scaffold construction at the end of assembly.
Total assembled sequence length in base pairs produced by the genome assembly process, measured after assembly completion; use the sum of contig or scaffold lengths as reported by the assembler.
N50 statistic in base pairs calculated for the assembled contigs or scaffolds at the end of the assembly process; larger values generally indicate more contiguous assemblies.
GC content percentage of the assembled genome produced by the assembly process, computed from the assembled sequence as a post-assembly summary metric.

Estimated completeness percentage of the assembled genome at the end of the assembly process, typically assessed with a benchmark set such as BUSCO; record the percentage of expected single-copy genes recovered.
Overall qualitative assessment of the assembly outcome at the process step, summarizing whether the assembled genome meets internal criteria for downstream biosynthetic gene cluster discovery.

assembled_genome.reasoning: The assembled_genome node is a Derivative, so I kept only computed-result fields that describe the final genome assembly object itself, while removing any field names that collided with earlier genome_assembly Process fields. I retained provenance, storage/file packaging, sequence count, completeness, and reuse readiness because these are derivative-level properties downstream users need. I excluded upstream read and process settings, and I renamed the assembly-wide summary fields to avoid repeating already generated names while preserving the same semantic content at the derivative layer.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed assembled genome object produced by the genome assembly process; use a stable code such as ASM_001. This identifies the derivative genome assembly used for downstream analyses.
Identifier of the upstream raw FASTQ data set used to compute this genome assembly, enabling provenance tracing from signal to derivative; format example: FASTQ_001.
File format of the assembled genome derivative as stored for downstream use; examples include fasta or fasta_gz. Record the format of the assembly artefact, not the input reads.
Size of the assembled genome file in bytes, measured from the stored derivative artefact after assembly completion; useful for data management and transfer validation.

Number of assembled sequences contained in the genome assembly derivative, typically corresponding to contigs or scaffolds depending on the stored representation; measured after assembly output generation.

Total length in base pairs of all sequences contained in the assembled genome derivative, measured from the final assembly artefact after computation; this is a derivative-level summary of genome span and should be recorded as the sum of all contig/scaffold lengths.
N50 statistic in base pairs calculated from the stored assembled genome derivative; this summarizes contiguity of the computed genome assembly and is evaluated after assembly generation.

GC content percentage computed from the assembled genome derivative, used as a sequence-composition summary of the final assembly artefact; measure after assembly completion from the stored derivative sequence.

Genome completeness percentage of the assembled genome derivative estimated from a benchmarking set such as BUSCO, recorded after the final assembly is produced; useful for judging suitability for downstream biosynthetic gene cluster discovery.
Boolean indicator of whether the assembled genome derivative is considered suitable for downstream BGC prediction and related reuse, based on internal thresholds for contiguity and completeness.

bgc_prediction.reasoning: The bgc_prediction node is a Process, so I included only how the scan for biosynthetic gene clusters was performed and the key process outcomes needed to interpret the prediction step. I focused on the prediction tool, version, rule set, cluster detection criteria, output counts, and confidence/quality summaries. I excluded genome assembly properties because those belong upstream, and I excluded the predicted BGC objects themselves because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided reusing previously generated assembly metric names that caused collisions, and instead used BGC-specific process outputs such as cluster count and average cluster length.

md_schema.descr: Name of the biosynthetic gene cluster prediction software used to scan the assembled fungal genome at this process step; example: antiSMASH.
Version of the biosynthetic gene cluster prediction software used during the scan; example: 7.0. Record the exact version to support reproducibility.
Rule set or detection mode applied during BGC prediction, recorded at the process step; examples include relaxed, strict, or fungal-specific modes depending on the software configuration.

Minimum genomic length in base pairs required for a region to be called as a biosynthetic gene cluster during prediction; this is a process threshold set before or during scanning, typically in the kilobase range.
Maximum allowed intergenic or inter-feature gap in base pairs when grouping genes into a predicted biosynthetic cluster, recorded as the process parameter used during scanning.
Number of biosynthetic gene clusters identified by the prediction process from the assembled genome, counted at the end of the scan before downstream annotation.
Average length in base pairs of the predicted biosynthetic gene clusters detected during the scan, measured from the set of predicted regions at the end of the process.
Boolean indicator of whether the prediction process detected a core scaffold or backbone biosynthetic gene in at least one cluster, used as a coarse process-quality summary for cluster discovery.

Qualitative confidence level assigned to the BGC prediction results at the end of the process, summarizing support for the called cluster set; use this to indicate whether the scan output is likely to be robust for downstream annotation.
Boolean flag indicating whether the BGC prediction run met internal quality criteria for downstream use, assessed after scanning the assembled genome and before annotation.

predicted_bgcs.reasoning: The predicted_bgcs node is a Derivative, so I kept only properties of the computed candidate cluster set itself: unique identity, provenance to the assembled genome, summary size/composition, output packaging, and a QC flag. I excluded prediction parameters because they belong to the bgc_prediction Process node, and I avoided the colliding field name predicted_bgc_count by replacing it with a more specific derivative-level summary tied to cluster architecture rather than a generic count. I also avoided using genome-level assembly metrics or downstream gene-level annotation properties, since those belong to other nodes.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed set of predicted biosynthetic gene clusters produced by the prediction process; use a stable code such as BGCSET_001. This identifies the derivative cluster set used for downstream annotation.
Identifier of the upstream assembled genome used to compute this predicted BGC set, enabling provenance tracing from assembly to cluster calls; format example: ASM_001.

Number of distinct genomic regions called as candidate biosynthetic gene clusters in this derivative set, measured after prediction output generation and before gene-level annotation; typical values depend on fungal genome size and biosynthetic richness.
Total genomic span in base pairs covered by all predicted biosynthetic gene cluster regions in this derivative set, computed from the final predicted intervals.

Mean length in base pairs of the predicted biosynthetic gene clusters contained in this derivative set, computed from the set after prediction completion; typical values may range from several kilobases to tens of kilobases.
Maximum cluster length in base pairs among the predicted biosynthetic gene clusters in the derivative set, measured from the final predicted intervals.
Total number of genes encompassed by all predicted biosynthetic gene clusters in the derivative set, counted from the computed cluster intervals after prediction.

Distribution of predicted biosynthetic gene cluster classes represented in the derivative set, recorded as a summary of the computed output; examples include terpene, polyketide, nonribosomal_peptide, and hybrid classes.
File or table format used to store the computed predicted BGC set for downstream analysis; examples include gff, csv, tsv, or json.
Overall quality flag for the predicted BGC derivative set, assigned after prediction output generation to summarize whether the cluster calls are suitable for downstream annotation.

cluster_annotation.reasoning: The cluster_annotation node is a Process, so I included only annotation workflow parameters and process-level outputs that describe how predicted clusters were functionally annotated. I focused on the annotation software, version, reference database, thresholds, and summary outcomes such as number of genes annotated and confidence metrics. I excluded upstream predicted-cluster identity and counts because those belong to the predicted_bgcs Derivative node, and I excluded downstream annotated-cluster artifacts because those belong to the annotated_clusters Derivative node. I also avoided field-name reuse by not repeating the already-generated predicted_bgc_count field, instead using annotation-specific summaries like annotated_gene_count and functional_assignment rate.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to annotate genes within predicted biosynthetic gene clusters at this process step; example: Prokka.
Version of the annotation software used during cluster annotation; example: 1.14. Record the exact version for reproducibility.
Name of the reference database used to infer gene functions and pathway roles during cluster annotation; examples include UniProt, Pfam, or custom fungal BGC databases.
Version or release date of the reference database used at the annotation step; format example: UniProt_2024_01 or Pfam 35.0.

Percent sequence-identity threshold applied when assigning gene function during cluster annotation, measured as a process parameter; typical values are in the 30-95 percent range depending on database and stringency.

Percent coverage threshold required for accepting a gene-level functional assignment in the cluster annotation process; typical values are in the 30-95 percent range depending on the annotation workflow.
Number of genes within the predicted clusters that received a functional or pathway-role annotation at the end of the annotation process.
Number of genes within the predicted clusters that remained without a confident functional assignment after annotation.
Percentage of genes in the predicted clusters that were assigned a functional role during annotation, calculated at the end of the process; this summarizes annotation success across the cluster set.

Qualitative confidence level summarizing the strength of gene-level annotations produced by this process; use this to indicate whether pathway-role assignments are robust enough for downstream interpretation.

annotated_clusters.reasoning: The annotated_clusters node is a Derivative, so I included only properties of the computed annotation result itself: derivative identity/provenance, annotation coverage summary, functional-class composition, output format, and reuse quality. I excluded annotation software and database parameters because those belong to the upstream cluster_annotation Process node, and I excluded raw predicted-cluster counts because those belong to the upstream predicted_bgcs Derivative node. I also avoided field-name collisions by not reusing the previously generated annotated_gene_count field; instead I used result-level summary fields specific to the annotated cluster derivative.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed gene-level annotated cluster set produced by the cluster annotation process; use a stable code such as ANNBGC_001. This identifies the derivative object containing the final annotations.
Identifier of the upstream predicted biosynthetic gene cluster set that was annotated to produce this derivative; format example: BGCSET_001.
Number of biosynthetic gene clusters present in this annotated derivative set, counted after annotation has been attached to the predicted clusters.
Percentage of genes within the annotated cluster set that carry a gene-level functional assignment in the final derivative, summarizing annotation coverage; report as a percentage from 0 to 100.

Distribution of functional categories assigned to genes within the annotated clusters, recorded as a summary of the derivative output; examples include backbone enzyme, tailoring enzyme, transport, regulation, resistance, and unknown.
File or table format used to store the annotated cluster derivative for downstream analysis; examples include gff3, json, tsv, or csv.

Free-text provenance note summarizing the main annotation reference or rule set encoded in the derivative, such as the database family or annotation pipeline version, when a compact provenance summary is needed at the result level.

Overall quality flag for the annotated cluster derivative, assigned after annotations are finalized to indicate whether the result is suitable for downstream biosynthetic interpretation and integration.

Qualitative assessment of how completely pathway roles were assigned across the annotated cluster set at the derivative stage, summarizing whether the final annotations capture the core biosynthetic logic.

fungal_biomass_metabolite.reasoning: The fungal_biomass_metabolite node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic specimen/source fields describing the fungal material reserved for metabolite work: identity, organism/strain provenance, collection state, storage, and whether it was specifically reserved for chemical profiling. I excluded extraction solvents, purification settings, and LC-MS parameters because those belong to downstream Process/Capture nodes, and I avoided duplicating any upstream biomass identifiers already established for the genome workflow. I also kept the metadata focused on the material state needed to interpret metabolite yields and provenance, not on any measured metabolite outputs.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the fungal biomass aliquot reserved for secondary metabolite extraction and profiling; use a stable sample code such as MBM_001. This identifies the entity used in the metabolomics branch of the workflow.
Scientific name of the fungal organism represented by the metabolite biomass, recorded for provenance of the chemical sample; format example: Aspergillus terreus.
Internal strain or isolate identifier for the fungal material reserved for metabolite analysis, if applicable; format example: isolate FUNG-17 or ATCC 12345.
Physical preservation state of the fungal biomass at the time it is reserved for metabolite extraction; examples include fresh, frozen, dried, or lyophilized.
Boolean indicator of whether this biomass aliquot was intentionally reserved for chemical extraction and profiling of secondary metabolites rather than genomic work.
Date on which the fungal biomass was set aside or designated for metabolite extraction and analysis; format YYYY-MM-DD.
Storage condition of the biomass reserved for metabolite work prior to extraction, recorded at the material level; examples include -80 C, liquid nitrogen, or desiccated room-temperature storage.
Context describing how the fungal biomass was obtained or cultured before being reserved for metabolomics, such as fermentation broth pellet, plate-grown colony, or harvested mycelium.

metabolite_extraction.reasoning: The metabolite_extraction node is a Process, so I included only how the solvent-based extraction was carried out and the key process outcome for reproducibility and yield assessment. I focused on solvent identity, solvent-to-biomass ratio, extraction mode, temperature, duration, number of cycles, and crude-extract yield/quality. I excluded biomass provenance because that belongs to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded crude extract file or storage properties because those belong to the downstream crude_extract Entity node. I also avoided any genome-branch terminology or reused identifiers, keeping the fields strictly within the metabolite extraction process territory.

md_schema.descr: Name of the primary solvent used to extract secondary metabolites from fungal material at this process step; examples include methanol, ethyl acetate, or acetone.

Volume of extraction solvent applied per gram of fungal material during the metabolite extraction process, measured at setup; report in milliliters per gram, typically ranging from 1 to 50 ml/g depending on protocol.
Mode of solvent contact used during metabolite extraction, recorded as the active process configuration; examples include maceration, sonication, shaking, or reflux.

Temperature in degrees Celsius maintained during solvent-based metabolite extraction, measured at the process step; typical values range from 4 to 80 Celsius depending on compound stability and protocol.
Total duration in minutes of the active metabolite extraction step, measured from solvent addition to completion of the extraction cycle; typical range is 5-1440 minutes.
Number of repeated solvent extraction cycles applied to the fungal material during the extraction process, counted at the end of the step; common values are 1-5 cycles.

Mass of crude extract recovered at the end of the metabolite extraction process, measured after solvent removal or concentration; report in milligrams, typically ranging from a few mg to grams depending on biomass input.
Observed color of the crude extract produced by the extraction process, recorded as a simple process-quality descriptor; examples include brown, yellow, green, or dark amber.
Boolean flag indicating whether the extraction yielded a crude extract suitable for downstream purification and chemical analysis, assessed at the end of the process step.

crude_extract.reasoning: The crude_extract node is an Entity, so I kept only intrinsic properties of the extracted metabolite mixture itself: identity/provenance, physical state, concentration, storage, and a simple composition summary. The earlier collision on storage_temperature_celsius means I must avoid reusing that field name here, so I replaced it with a more specific storage field for the crude extract entity. I excluded extraction protocol variables because those belong to the upstream metabolite_extraction Process node, and I excluded purification and LC-MS details because those belong downstream.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the crude metabolite extract entity produced by the extraction process; use a stable code such as CRD_001. This identifies the metabolite mixture before purification and analysis.
Identifier of the upstream fungal biomass reserved for metabolite work from which this crude extract was produced; format example: MBM_001.

Qualitative indication of whether significant solvent residue remains in the crude extract entity after concentration or drying, recorded before purification; examples include dry, trace_residual_solvent, or wet.

Measured concentration of the crude metabolite extract entity after concentration and before purification; report in milligrams per milliliter, typically ranging from low fractions to tens of mg/ml depending on resuspension.
Total mass of crude metabolite extract available as the entity after extraction and concentration, measured before fractionation; report in milligrams.

Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the crude extract entity is stored prior to purification or analysis; examples include -20 or -80 Celsius. This field is specific to the crude extract entity to avoid collision with other workflow storage metadata.
Solvent or buffer used to store or resuspend the crude extract entity before purification or analysis; examples include methanol, acetonitrile, or dimethyl sulfoxide.

Brief qualitative note describing the apparent composition of the crude extract entity prior to purification, such as pigmented, lipid-rich, or highly complex mixture. This is a lightweight entity-level characterization rather than a process parameter.

metabolite_purification.reasoning: The metabolite_purification node is a Process, so I included only how the crude extract was fractionated and the process-level outcomes needed to interpret purification success. I focused on purification method, stationary/mobile phase details where relevant, fractionation settings, number of fractions, enrichment, and purification yield/QC. I excluded crude extract intrinsic properties because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded purified fraction storage or file-like properties because those belong to the downstream purified_metabolites Entity node. I also avoided field-name collisions by not using the already-generated storage_temperature_celsius field and instead kept the temperature field specific to the purification process.

md_schema.descr: Primary fractionation or cleanup method used to purify the crude extract at this process step; examples include solid-phase extraction, silica chromatography, liquid-liquid partitioning, or preparative HPLC.
Stationary phase or column material used during purification, recorded at the process step when chromatography is involved; examples include C18, silica, or Sephadex.
Primary mobile phase or solvent system used during metabolite purification, recorded as the active process chemistry; examples include water-acetonitrile gradients or hexane-ethyl acetate mixtures.

Temperature in degrees Celsius maintained during the purification process, measured at the step where fractionation is performed; typical values range from 4 to 30 Celsius depending on compound stability.

Number of fractionation or collection steps applied to the crude extract during purification, counted over the full process; typical values are 1 or more depending on the level of resolution required.
Total number of purified fractions collected from the crude extract at the end of the purification process; this is a process output summary, not a property of the downstream fraction entity.

Estimated enrichment factor of target secondary metabolite components achieved by purification relative to the crude extract, measured at the end of the process; report as fold enrichment when available.
Percentage of initial crude extract mass recovered after purification, calculated at the end of the process to summarize material loss during fractionation.
Qualitative assessment of whether the purification process produced fractions of sufficient cleanliness for downstream chemical analysis, evaluated at the end of the process step.

purified_metabolites.reasoning: The purified_metabolites node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the purified fraction material itself: identifier and provenance, fraction identity, purity, concentration, composition, storage, and whether the fraction is ready for LC-MS. I excluded purification method and chromatographic settings because those belong to the upstream metabolite_purification Process node, and I excluded LC-MS instrument settings because those belong downstream to the lcms_capture Capture node. I also avoided reusing the already-generated storage_temperature_celsius field by using fraction-specific storage metadata only where needed and keeping the schema focused on the purified chemical entity.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the purified metabolite fraction entity produced by the purification process; use a stable code such as PF_001. This identifies the fraction that will be used for chemical profiling or further isolation.
Identifier of the upstream crude extract from which this purified fraction was derived; format example: CRD_001.
Ordinal number or label of the purified fraction within the purification series, assigned at collection; example values include F1, F2, or 3 depending on the fractionation scheme.
Estimated purity percentage of the purified metabolite fraction, measured after purification and before chemical analysis; report as 0 to 100 percent.

Measured concentration of the purified fraction entity before LC-MS analysis or further isolation; report in milligrams per milliliter, typically lower than crude extract but enriched for target compounds.
Number of candidate secondary metabolites believed to be present in the purified fraction based on purification context and pre-analysis assessment; this is an entity-level composition summary.
Storage condition of the purified metabolite fraction before LC-MS analysis, recorded at the material level; examples include -20 C, -80 C, or protected from light.
Boolean indicator of whether the purified fraction must be protected from light during storage or handling to preserve metabolite integrity.
Boolean indicator of whether the purified metabolite fraction is considered ready for LC-MS capture based on purity, concentration, and handling status.

Brief qualitative note describing the main chemical characteristics of the purified fraction, such as enriched pigment, dominant alkaloid-like fraction, or mixed metabolite fraction. This is an entity-level characterization rather than a process parameter.

lcms_capture.reasoning: The lcms_capture node is a Capture node, so I included only instrument configuration and measurement-session settings that were actively controlled during LC-MS analysis: vendor/model/serial, run ID, chromatography and MS acquisition settings, and run-quality metrics. I excluded properties of the purified metabolite fractions because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded file-level properties because those belong to the downstream raw_lcms Signal node. I also kept the fields focused on active capture parameters rather than interpretation or processed-feature outputs, which are downstream of this session.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the LC-MS instrument used for the chemical profiling capture session, recorded as the hardware vendor controlling the measurement; example: Thermo Fisher Scientific or Agilent.
Model name of the LC-MS instrument used for the chemical profiling capture session; example: Q Exactive Orbitrap. Record the actual platform used to acquire the raw chemical profiles.
Instrument serial number for the LC-MS system used in this capture session, recorded to uniquely identify the hardware unit; format example: LCMS123456.
Unique identifier of the LC-MS acquisition session that produced the raw chemical profiles; use a stable run code such as LCMS_RUN_001.
Column chemistry or type configured for the LC-MS capture session, recorded at run setup; examples include C18, HILIC, or phenyl-hexyl.
Total LC gradient duration in minutes configured for the capture session, measured from injection to end of chromatographic separation; typical values range from 5 to 120 minutes.
Composition of mobile phase A used in the LC-MS capture session, recorded as the active chromatographic solvent system; examples include water with 0.1 percent formic acid or ammonium acetate buffer.
Composition of mobile phase B used in the LC-MS capture session, recorded as the active chromatographic solvent system; examples include acetonitrile with 0.1 percent formic acid or methanol.
Ionization mode configured on the mass spectrometer during the capture session, recorded as the active acquisition setting; allowed values reflect the polarity used for metabolite detection.
Mass-to-charge range configured for MS acquisition during the LC-MS capture session, measured in m/z and set at run time; typical metabolomics ranges are broad, such as 50-1500 m/z.
MS/MS acquisition strategy configured during the capture session, such as data-dependent or data-independent acquisition, used to generate fragment spectra when applicable.
Injection volume in microliters used for the LC-MS capture session, measured at run setup; typical values are low microliter volumes such as 1-20 ul.

Autosampler or source temperature in degrees Celsius actively controlled during the capture session, measured at the instrument setup stage; typical values range from 4 to 60 Celsius depending on platform.
Qualitative stability assessment of the total ion chromatogram across the LC-MS capture session, used as a run-level quality indicator after acquisition.
Boolean flag indicating whether the LC-MS capture session met internal quality-control criteria for downstream metabolomics processing, assessed after the run completes.

raw_lcms.reasoning: The raw_lcms node is a Signal, so I kept only artifact-level properties of the raw LC-MS files and removed any fields that collide with previously generated raw-data metadata from the genomic branch. I retained LC-MS-specific file identity, format, scan dimensions, chromatographic ranges, and technical quality metrics, while excluding instrument settings and downstream processed feature information. I also replaced generic file-management fields that had collisions (file_size_bytes and checksum_md5) with LC-MS-specific storage integrity fields so the schema remains unique across the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw LC-MS data file or run output produced by the capture session; use a stable code such as LCMS_001. This identifies the raw chemical signal artifact itself.
Digital file format of the raw LC-MS signal artifact, recorded after acquisition; examples include mzML, mzXML, or vendor-specific proprietary formats.
Number of chromatographic runs or sample injections represented in the raw LC-MS artefact, counted from the file contents after acquisition. For single injections this is typically one per file.

Total number of mass spectral scans contained in the raw LC-MS artefact, counted from the file contents after acquisition; typically ranges from thousands to hundreds of thousands depending on run length.

Observed retention time range in minutes covered by the raw LC-MS artefact, describing the acquisition time span captured in the file; record as the total chromatographic runtime or the min-max range as stored.
Observed mass-to-charge range in m/z represented in the raw LC-MS signal, reflecting the acquisition span stored in the file; example format: 50-1500 m/z.
Aggregate signal-to-noise metric computed directly from the raw LC-MS artefact as a technical quality indicator; report the platform- or file-level metric used by the acquisition software.
File system path or object-storage URI where the raw LC-MS data are stored after acquisition transfer; example formats include /data/lcms/run1.raw or s3://bucket/path/sample.mzML.

SHA-256 checksum of the raw LC-MS file used to verify data integrity after transfer or storage; format example: 64-character hexadecimal digest. This is a signal-level integrity field specific to LC-MS to avoid collisions with other DAG steps.

Version or revision string of the vendor acquisition file wrapper or conversion container associated with the raw LC-MS data, recorded for technical provenance; example: 3.2.1 or vendor build identifier.

metabolomics_processing.reasoning: The metabolomics_processing node is a Process, so I included only how raw LC-MS data were converted into aligned features and putative compound identifications, plus process-level parameters and output quality indicators. I focused on software, version, peak-picking and alignment settings, feature/compound summary counts, and identification confidence. I excluded raw LC-MS file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting feature table object because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided field-name collisions by not reusing generic file metrics already generated elsewhere.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to process raw LC-MS data into aligned features and putative compound identifications at this process step; example: MZmine.
Version of the metabolomics processing software used during feature detection and alignment; example: 3.0. Record the exact version for reproducibility.
Peak-picking algorithm or method used to detect LC-MS features from raw spectra at the processing step; examples include centroiding, wavelet-based detection, or local minimum search.

Method used to align retention times across LC-MS runs during processing, recorded as the active workflow setting; examples include linear alignment, loess-based alignment, or reference-based alignment.
Mass-to-charge tolerance in parts per million used during feature grouping and identification at the processing step; typical values are in the low single digits to tens of ppm.
Number of aligned LC-MS features detected after processing the raw data, counted at the end of the workflow step before derivative table creation.
Number of LC-MS features assigned a putative compound identity during processing, measured at the end of the step after matching against databases or rules.
Minimum score required for accepting a putative compound identification from MS/MS matching or spectral library search during processing; typical values depend on the scoring system used.
Boolean flag indicating whether the aligned feature set met internal quality criteria at the end of metabolomics processing, such as consistent retention-time alignment and acceptable missingness.

Qualitative confidence category summarizing the strength of putative compound identifications produced by the processing step; use this to distinguish high-confidence matches from tentative assignments.

compound_features.reasoning: The compound_features node is a Derivative, so I included only properties of the computed feature table itself: derivative identity/provenance, table size and structure, feature-level summary metrics, identification summaries, and output/QC status. I excluded software and algorithm settings because those belong to the upstream metabolomics_processing Process node, and I excluded raw LC-MS file properties because those belong to the upstream raw_lcms Signal node. I also avoided field-name collisions by not reusing generic feature_count or file metrics already introduced elsewhere, instead using table-specific summary fields for the derived compound feature object.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed compound feature table derivative produced from processed LC-MS data; use a stable code such as CF_001. This identifies the downstream table of detected features and inferred compound identities.
Identifier of the upstream raw LC-MS data set used to compute this compound feature table, enabling provenance tracing from signal to derivative; format example: LCMS_001.
Number of rows in the compound feature table, counted after derivative table creation; typically one row per aligned feature or feature-annotation pair depending on table design.
Number of columns in the compound feature table, counted from the final derivative object; this summarizes the structural complexity of the output table.
Number of aligned metabolite features represented in the derived table, counted from the final processed feature set after table construction.
Number of features in the table that carry a putative or inferred compound identity in the final derivative, measured after annotation has been attached.
Percentage of aligned features in the derived table that have an inferred compound identity, calculated from the final table as a summary of annotation coverage.
Storage format of the computed compound feature derivative table; examples include tsv, csv, xlsx, or parquet.
Overall quality flag for the compound feature derivative, assigned after table construction to indicate whether the output is suitable for downstream integrative analysis.

Summary of major metabolite classes represented among the inferred compound identities in the derived table, recorded as a high-level result description; examples include polyketides, peptides, alkaloids, and terpenoids.

integrative_analysis.reasoning: The integrative_analysis node is a Process, so I included only how the gene-cluster annotations and metabolite features were linked and the process-level outputs that summarize the inferred relationships. I focused on linkage method, matching criteria, network/scoring settings, numbers of links and pairs, and confidence summaries. I excluded upstream annotated cluster and compound feature properties because those belong to the input Derivative nodes, and I excluded the final association table because that belongs to the downstream biosynthetic_links Derivative node. I also avoided reusing field names already generated for feature or cluster counts by keeping the metrics specific to cross-omics linkage rather than source-table summary counts.

md_schema.descr: Method used to associate annotated biosynthetic gene clusters with metabolite features at this process step; examples include correlation-based linking, co-occurrence, manual curation, or network-based matching.

Minimum correlation coefficient or analogous association threshold used to accept a cluster-feature link during integrative analysis; report the numeric threshold applied by the workflow, typically between 0 and 1 when correlation-based.

Mass-to-charge matching tolerance in parts per million used when aligning metabolite features to candidate biosynthetic products during integrative analysis; typical values are in the low single digits to tens of ppm.
Maximum retention time window in minutes allowed when linking metabolite features to biosynthetic clusters during the integrative analysis step; this is a process parameter set to constrain matching.
Number of biosynthetic cluster to metabolite feature pairs linked by the integrative analysis process, counted at the end of the workflow step.
Number of cluster-feature associations classified as high confidence by the integrative analysis process, counted after scoring and filtering are complete.
Minimum association score required for a cluster-feature link to be retained in the integrative analysis output; report the numeric threshold used by the workflow.

Qualitative summary category of the evidence supporting inferred biosynthetic relationships in this process step, used to summarize how strongly the linked clusters and metabolite features support a pathway connection.
Boolean flag indicating whether the integrative analysis met internal quality criteria for producing downstream biosynthetic associations, assessed after linkage and scoring are complete.

biosynthetic_links.reasoning: The biosynthetic_links node is a Derivative, so I included only properties of the integrated result set itself: derivative identity/provenance, number and type of links, confidence and evidence summaries, output format, and overall quality. I excluded the linkage algorithm and thresholds because those belong to the upstream integrative_analysis Process node, and I excluded source cluster/feature table summaries because those belong to the upstream annotated_clusters and compound_features derivatives. I also avoided field-name collisions by using result-specific association terms rather than generic cluster or feature count fields already used elsewhere.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the integrated biosynthetic association result set produced by the integrative analysis process; use a stable code such as LINKSET_001. This identifies the derivative object connecting gene clusters to metabolite features.
Identifier of the upstream annotated cluster set used as one input to produce this integrated association set; format example: ANNBGC_001.
Identifier of the upstream compound feature table used as the other input to produce this integrated association set; format example: CF_001.
Total number of inferred cluster-to-metabolite associations contained in the integrated derivative set, counted after integrative analysis completion.
Number of unique biosynthetic gene clusters represented among the integrated associations in the derivative set, counted from the final links.
Number of unique metabolite features represented among the integrated associations in the derivative set, counted from the final links.
Qualitative summary of the evidence type supporting the integrated biosynthetic links, recorded at the derivative stage; examples include coexpression, cooccurrence, mass match, or manual curation.
Percentage of links in the integrated derivative set classified as high confidence, calculated from the final association set and used as a quality summary for downstream interpretation.
File or table format used to store the integrated biosynthetic association derivative for downstream use; examples include tsv, csv, json, or graphml.

Overall quality flag for the integrated biosynthetic link derivative, assigned after final association construction to indicate whether the result is suitable for reporting or follow-on hypothesis testing.
